one_line: Floor-plan editor where agents propose changes and humans alone commit them.
what_it_does: Provides a multiplayer spatial editor with forked agent proposals, human review, and compile-time protection of the committed plan.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is integral to a structured proposal surface in which agents can edit a fork but cannot access committed state; this collaboration is not comparably safe through generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About text says tools receive only a proposal-layer capability and writes to committed state fail to compile.
Frames visibly show agent proposals, human commit count, and compile failure.
execution_rationale: The central safety workflow is visibly demonstrated, including proposal state and an explicit compile-time rejection, with a coherent floor-plan UI.
execution_evidence: Frames show 'AGENTS PROPOSE. HUMANS COMMIT.' and 'IT FAILS TO COMPILE.'
Description includes source-tree enforcement test and scoped capability design.
impact_rationale: Shared spatial planning benefits from reviewable, reversible agent edits; structural protection addresses a real trust problem.
impact_evidence: Floor plans make harmful changes immediately inspectable.
Human approval and egress validation are part of the described workflow.
creativity_rationale: Compile-time enforcement of human-only commit in a spatial editor is unusually original and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: Proposal/commit separation is the product's core interaction model.
Visible compile failure demonstrates the concept rather than merely stating it.
usability_note: Reviewable diffs and visible spatial edits support understanding; proposal layers may add complexity.
red_flags: The attempted change shown fails compilation, so successful commit is not demonstrated.
standouts: Safety guarantee is structural, not a prompt or policy.
Agent and human permissions are reflected in the UI.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and creativity with strong visible evidence of the defining safety mechanism.
